question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, what is the maximum number of times you may exit the vehicle to check its position (a 'look'), except for the Straight Line Backing exercise?
explanation: The manual states the maximum number of times you may look to check the position of your vehicle is two (2), except for the Straight Line Backing exercise, which allows only one look.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: For the Straight Line Backing exercise specifically, how many 'looks' (exits from the vehicle to check its position) are you allowed?
explanation: Straight Line Backing is the exception to the general two-look rule for skills test exercises; the manual allows only one look for this specific exercise.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: Before you exit the vehicle to check its external position during a skills test exercise, what must you do?
choice_c: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s)
explanation: The manual requires that when safely stopping and exiting the vehicle to check its position, you must place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s) before exiting.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: During the skills test, what is scored as a 'pull-up'?
choice_a: Stopping the vehicle without changing direction
choice_d: A driver stopping and pulling forward to clear an encroachment or get a better position
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as when a driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or to get a better position; it specifically notes that stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: What is scored as an 'encroachment' during the basic vehicle control skills test?
choice_a: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle
choice_b: Taking more than the allowed number of looks
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle, with each encroachment counting as an error.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: In the Alley Dock exercise, how close must the rear of your vehicle come to the rear of the alley, without touching boundary lines or cones?
explanation: The manual states you must back into the alley, bringing the rear of your vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley, without touching boundary lines or cones.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: In the Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise, on which side of your vehicle is the parking space located?
explanation: The manual describes the Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise as parking in a space that is on your left, distinguishing it from the Conventional parallel park, which is on your right.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: According to the Vermont CDL manual, when is 'unsafe coasting' occurring as you approach a turn?
choice_a: Whenever the vehicle exceeds the posted speed limit
choice_b: Whenever the turn signal is not used
choice_c: Whenever the driver brakes more than once
choice_d: Whenever the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: As you come to a stop behind a stop sign, signal, or stop line at an intersection, what is required regarding your vehicle's movement?
choice_a: Your vehicle must not roll forward or backward
choice_b: Allow slight rolling forward if traffic is clear
choice_c: Coast to the stop line to save fuel
choice_d: Keep the vehicle in gear with the clutch fully engaged the whole time
explanation: The manual states that when coming to a complete stop behind a stop sign, signal, sidewalk, or stop line, your vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: During the 'Urban Business' portion of the on-road test, where should your vehicle be positioned and how should your speed be managed?
choice_a: Centered in the left-most lane, exceeding traffic flow when possible
choice_b: Centered in the right-most lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_c: Straddling two lanes to allow for turns
choice_d: In any lane, at a constant 25 mph
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (the right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: If you are driving a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards, at what distance must you stop before a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 25 feet but not less than 10 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: Within 100 feet but not less than 25 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Exactly 20 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual requires such drivers to stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail when approaching a railroad crossing.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: When performing a student discharge in a school bus, how far away from students at the stop must the bus come to a complete stop?
explanation: The manual states you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop before beginning the discharge procedure.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: If your vehicle is equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, what must you do when shifting during the on-road test?
choice_b: Rev the engine before each shift
choice_c: Ride the clutch to control speed
choice_d: Coast with the clutch depressed between gears
explanation: The manual requires that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting, and warns against revving or lugging the engine, riding the clutch, or coasting with the clutch depressed.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: Under the Lane Usage scoring category, in which lane should you finish a left turn on a multiple lane road?
choice_b: The lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_d: The lane closest to the shoulder
explanation: The manual specifies that a left turn on a multiple lane road should finish in the lane directly to the right of the center line, while a right turn should finish in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: When resuming driving after the Stop/Start maneuver and releasing the parking brake, what should you avoid doing?
choice_c: Turning the wheel before your vehicle moves
explanation: The manual instructs that when traffic permits and you release the parking brake to pull straight ahead, you should not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving

question: When approaching a curve, why should you reduce your speed before entering it, according to the manual?
choice_a: So you can accelerate through the curve for stability
choice_b: So you can shift into a higher gear mid-curve
choice_c: So you can safely change lanes within the curve
choice_d: So that further braking or shifting is not required once in the curve
explanation: The manual states that before entering a curve you should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving
